title: Imposes Section 201 Tariffs on Solar Panels and Washing Machines
description_short: Trump issued a proclamation imposing safeguard tariffs on imported solar cells and washing machines.
description_medium: On January 23, 2018, President Trump issued a proclamation applying Section 201 safeguard tariffs to imported solar cells and modules and large residential washing machines. The measure covered two product groups: solar equipment and large household washers. Tariff rates, product exclusions and duration would determine which imports faced added costs.
organization_tags: Office of the U.S. Trade Representative

title: Government Shutdown Ends After 35 Days
description_short: Trump agreed to reopen the government after the longest shutdown in U.S. history without securing wall funding.
description_medium: On January 25, 2019, Trump agreed to reopen the federal government after a 35-day shutdown without securing the border-wall funding he had demanded. The agreement ended the immediate closure and left the funding dispute unresolved. The shutdown became the longest in U.S. history, while no permanent agreement on wall funding was reached.

title: Removes Pentagon IG Glenn Fine from Oversight
description_short: Trump removed Pentagon inspector general Glenn Fine from the panel overseeing pandemic relief oversight.
description_medium: On April 7, 2020, President Trump removed Pentagon Inspector General Glenn Fine from the committee overseeing pandemic relief. Fine had been selected to lead the Pandemic Response Accountability Committee, which was created to monitor federal coronavirus spending. The removal took him out of the role leading an independent panel created to track federal relief spending.

title: Pardons Mary Ballard McCarty
description_short: Trump granted a presidential pardon to Mary Ballard McCarty as part of a clemency list.
description_medium: On January 19, 2021, President Donald Trump granted a pardon to Mary Ballard McCarty, whose case was in the Southern District of Florida. The Justice Department lists her 2009 sentence as 42 months in prison, three years of supervised release and a $100,000 fine for conspiracy to commit honest-services fraud.
description_long: On January 19, 2021, President Donald Trump granted a pardon to Mary Ballard McCarty, whose federal case was in the Southern District of Florida. The Justice Department’s clemency record lists a 42-month prison sentence, three years of supervised release and a $100,000 fine imposed in 2009 for conspiracy to commit honest-services fraud. The pardon appeared among the grants issued during the final days of Trump’s first term. A presidential pardon is an act of executive clemency for a federal offense; it does not amount to a new trial or erase the historical record of the conviction. The announcement did not explain why McCarty was selected. A pardon can remove some collateral consequences of a federal conviction, but it does not turn the underlying proceedings into an acquittal or erase the court record.
organization_tags: U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Florida
